newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB's Elstein joins Channel 5 as CEO.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB's Elstein joins Channel 5 as CEO.

text.p: David Elstein, head of programming at BSkyB, is leaving the company to become Chief Executive Officer of Britain's new fifth terrestrial television channel, its owners Channel 5 Broadcasting said on Friday.
Channel 5, Britain's fifth terrestrial television channel, is scheduled to begin broadcasting in January 1997.
Its shareholders are British companies Pearson and United News and Media, broadcast group CLT of Luxembourg and U.S. investment group Warburg Pincus.
Elstein will join the board of Channel 5 Broadcasting with immediate effect and take up his new role on September 16.
He has been head of programming at BSkyB, Britain's biggest pay television operator, since January 1993.
Ian Ritchie, Channel 5 chief executive since last October, will continue with the company as chief operating officer.

"This appointment is excellent news for Channel 5. David Elstein is one of Britain's most talented and respected broadcasting executives, and will bring significant additional strength to C5B's management team," said Frank Barlow, chairman of Channel 5 Broadcasting.
"He has long been an enthusiastic advocate of a fifth channel and has a deep understanding of its potential in the new broadcasting environment," added Barlow.
Elstein, 51, began his career as a graudate trainee at the BBC before joining commercial Thames Television as a producer/director.
He worked for ITV's LWT and a number of independent production companies before becoming Director of Programmes at Thames in 1986.
His stint at BSkyB has been a successful one, the satellite broadcaster building a base of over five million subscribers thanks to its diet of Hollywood blockbusters and top-rating sports events.
